title: Readiness, as every surface reports it
notes: Drives all seven readiness surfaces from one set of facts per cohort student through src/lib/progression/readiness-consumers.ts, the Prisma-free home of the mapping the product actually uses. Ticket D1 (2026-09-07, owner-approved: 'live rows win everywhere') unified the three mappings this suite used to compare into one — `progressionStateReadiness` and `rosterReadiness` are now thin wrappers around `reconciledReadiness`, and the roster's readiness score plus the class-progress panel's now come from a batched loader (`fetchReadinessDataForStudents`) that reconciles live certification, portfolio, resume and shared-page rows instead of trusting the stored `Progression.state` alone. `consumer_disagreements` accordingly moved from `info` (116 of 300 pairs, floor null) to a real gate at `floor: 0` — a future consumer registered under any mapping name gets the same reconciled behaviour by construction, so a regression here means a surface actually diverged, not that a product call is still open. `denominator_is_all_items` reads the five production queries that supply the orientation denominator and is 0 if any grew a `where` — the 2026-07-31 decision ('readiness counts ALL orientation items on every surface') lived in the QUERY, so a source check is what can catch it coming back. `score_decreases_on_completion` is the design's monotonicity half: completing an orientation item must never lower a score. Floors read in each metric's own direction; `denominator_is_all_items` is 1 or 0, so a floor of 1 means 'no offender'.
